//catalog-growth-correction: CORRECTION (issue #674). Several notes below justify a budget bump with the claim that adding copy to the root next-intl catalog 'lands in the shared chunk and so costs every route about 1 kB'. That claim is wrong and should not be reused as precedent. It appears earliest in the top-level //-note above, for #476 re-baseline (in different wording, which is why the #929 sweep missed it -- see #948); it was then written in //media-picker, cited by //multi-creator, and //planner-serving-allocations rests on the same reasoning. Message catalogs do not contribute to First Load JS. Evidence: (1) a production build was searched for distinctive strings from three namespaces (mediaPicker, pwa, common) -- zero matches in .next/static/**/*.js, matches only in .next/server/chunks/*.js, because src/app/layout.tsx passes messages to NextIntlClientProvider as a prop, so they are serialized into the per-request RSC flight payload rather than compiled into a client chunk; (2) the / route is a clean control -- it renders no image field and no co-creator UI, and it has not moved (224.0 kB on a local Windows build) across both the mediaPicker and the recipeCreators catalog additions, though the claim predicts +1 kB for each. What actually moved those routes was code, not copy: the ~1 kB was ImageUploadField / media-picker-config wiring, which per-route module analysis found on exactly the three routes that grew and absent from /. The budget numbers below are NOT changed by this correction -- they were re-baselined to values that the measured routes genuinely need, so the limits are sound even though the stated reasoning was not. Only the diagnosis is corrected. The real cost of catalog growth is RSC payload transfer and hydration, which this gate does not measure at all; per-route message scoping is tracked in #674. Note the constraint any such change faces: use-intl's IntlProvider replaces messages on nesting rather than merging them, so a nested provider carrying only route namespaces would drop the globals. Before bumping a budget for 'catalog growth' again, measure which modules entered the route.

//lucide-1x: Issue #988 (lucide-react 0.475.0 -> 1.27.0). / is re-baselined 225 -> 228 and the / measurement claim below moves 225 -> 226. WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED, including the part that refutes how this note was first written. A same-commit A/B on one local Windows machine, differing only in the installed lucide version, moved exactly one tracked route: /recipes 252.0 -> 253.0, with / (225.0), /recipes/[cook]/[recipe] (308.0) and /recipes/[cook]/[recipe]/edit (218.0) identical across both builds. This note originally called those three 'controls' and concluded the bump does not touch the zero-headroom routes. THAT CONCLUSION WAS FALSE and CI refuted it: on Linux, main (ca04c615, run 31612285966) reads / at 225.0 and this branch reads / at 226.0, while /recipes reads 253.0 on BOTH. So the two platforms disagree about WHICH route the bump moved -- Windows says /recipes, Linux says /. Neither is wrong. 'next build' prints First Load JS as whole kB at this magnitude, so a sub-kB increase is invisible until it crosses an integer boundary, and the boundary sits at a different fractional offset on each platform. The general lesson, which is the reason this paragraph is longer than the numbers warrant: AT THIS RESOLUTION, 'WHICH ROUTE MOVED' IS NOT A STABLE FACT, AND AN UNCHANGED ROUTE IS NOT A CONTROL. An unchanged reading means 'gained less than the distance to the next integer', not 'gained nothing', and those two are indistinguishable in the output. A local A/B can show a bump is at least this large; it can never show a zero-headroom route is safe, because the safe case and the about-to-tip case print the same number. Do not repeat the inference this note originally made. The route budget for / therefore moves 225 -> 228, which is the measured 226 plus the 2 kB //headroom-requirement minimum, replacing a zero-headroom budget rather than restoring one -- zero headroom on / is a pre-existing condition this bump exposed rather than created. /recipes, /recipes/[cook]/[recipe] and /recipes/[cook]/[recipe]/edit are NOT bumped: Linux measures them at 253/308/218, unchanged from main, and inheriting a tight budget is not a failure.
//headroom-requirement: Issue #796: a budget that is NEW or RAISED must leave at least 2 kB above the value the same run measures, or the gate fails and names the minimum acceptable number. Budgets you do not touch are never subject to this — inheriting an existing tight budget is not a failure, and three routes below sit at zero headroom for exactly that reason. Size a new budget from CI figures, not local ones: Linux reads about 1 kB above a local Windows build, and 'next build' prints whole kB, so a sub-kB webpack redistribution can move a route a full displayed kilobyte with no code change (measured at 145 bytes in #789). The 2 kB is the same band the NEAR warning uses, so a budget that passes this check is one the warning will stay quiet about. The check needs the base ref's copy of this file; when it cannot be read it SKIPS rather than fails.

//measured.//: Machine-checked measurement claims (#858). check-bundle-budget.mjs verifies each of these against the same build that enforces the budgets below, and FAILS when one no longer matches. The prose notes above explain reasoning; these entries are what CI holds to reality. Four claims in this file have been corrected after the fact -- #674/#690, #763, #820 and #857 -- each found by a person who happened to look, because nothing compared them to a build. A claim is only about the platform that produced it: Linux CI reads ~1 kB above a local Windows build, so entries for other platforms are skipped rather than failed, and an entry with no platform fails as malformed. Update the number and the runId together; a value you cannot re-derive is a value you cannot audit. This guard closes DECAY only -- it compares a claim's kb to a build and never reads the prose around it, so it would have caught #820 and could not have caught #674, #763 or #857, where the number was already right. Attributing a regression to a module is a human obligation: see docs/performance-budgets.md.

//zero-headroom-variance:
Issue #996 (main went red at 96bbac61 with no code change). /recipes/[cook]/[recipe] is re-baselined 308 -> 312. WHAT WAS MEASURED, on Linux CI, for the SAME route across four runs:

  run 31476537117              308    (the original #820 claim)
  PR #995,  a7b8a7a3           308
  main,     96bbac61  <- RED   309
  PR #997,  3802856d           308

96bbac61's parent is a704dd49 with nothing landing in between, so the red run and PR #995's green run built a BYTE-IDENTICAL TREE on the same platform and disagreed by a full displayed kilobyte. The merge in between added no client bytes: cuid2 is server-only, and a search of the built client chunks -- run with a lucide/useState positive control, so a null result was distinguishable from a broken search -- finds no bignumber, BigNumber, error-causes or createId. The only cuid hits are Zod's own z.string().cuid() validator kind names.

THE CAUSE IS ROUNDING, NOT DRIFT, AND THE OTHER THREE ROUTES PROVE IT. Across those same runs / read 226.0, /recipes read 253.0 and /recipes/[cook]/[recipe]/edit read 218.0 EVERY TIME. A systematic push-vs-pull_request difference would have moved all four; only this one moved. Its true first-load size therefore sits near a half-kilobyte boundary, so Math.round lands on 308 or 309 depending on sub-100-byte chunk redistribution, while routes further from a boundary stay put.

THIS EXTENDS //lucide-1x RATHER THAN REPEATING IT. That note establishes that two PLATFORMS can disagree about which route moved, because 'next build' prints whole kB and the integer boundary sits at a different fractional offset on each platform. This is the same instrument failing one step further in: THE SAME TREE ON THE SAME PLATFORM MEASURED 308 AND 309 IN TWO RUNS. A budget at zero headroom is therefore not merely tight, it is a latent failure needing no code change to fire.

The new budget is the measured 309, plus the 2 kB //headroom-requirement minimum, plus 1 kB for the rounding flip measured here: sizing it at exactly 311 would satisfy the rule while leaving nothing to absorb the very effect that caused this failure.

KNOWN LIMITATION, FILED SEPARATELY: the #858 claim below is strict equality against Math.round, so for a route straddling a rounding boundary no single integer is stable -- this run measures 308 and the run that produced the red measured 309. The claim is recorded at 308, the value three of the four runs above produced, which means a future run that reads 309 will fail the claim (though NOT the budget, which now has room for it). Widening #858 to express a boundary tolerance is a change to the guard's semantics and is left as its own decision rather than made in passing here.

/recipes/[cook]/[recipe]/edit remains at 218/218 with 0.0 kB free and is expected to fail this way eventually, but it is deliberately NOT bumped -- nothing measured it as needing a raise, and inheriting a tight budget is not a failure.

Issue #1047 moves ONE measurement claim: /recipes 253 -> 254 (run 32103794242). NO BUDGET IS TOUCHED -- 255 stands and the route keeps 1.0 kB free. The cost is always-on client UI on the search route: the macro filter selects and chips, the withheld-results disclosure banner, and the per-card figure line. Do not reach for the catalog explanation //catalog-growth-correction forbids; ~17 new keys x 4 locales ship with this change and they are not the cause.

THE SECOND HALF OF THIS NOTE IS THE USEFUL PART, and it is about a claim this PR ended up NOT changing. /recipes/[cook]/[recipe] read 310 on the first CI run of this branch (32103794242) against a claim of 309, and 309 on the next run (32104326079). Between those two runs THE ONLY CHANGE WAS TO THIS FILE -- no client code, no dependency, nothing that reaches a chunk. So the claim was briefly edited to 310 and is now restored to its original 309 / run 32086887202 / #1029 entry, unchanged from main.

THIS IS THE EXACT FAILURE //zero-headroom-variance PREDICTED, OBSERVED AGAIN AND MORE CHEAPLY. That note recorded a byte-identical tree reading 308 and 309 across two runs and warned in its KNOWN LIMITATION that strict equality has no stable integer for a route straddling a rounding boundary. Here that route has now printed 307, 308, 309 and 310 across five runs. The prediction was not merely reconfirmed, it FIRED ON A DOC-ONLY COMMIT, which is the cheapest possible demonstration that the reading is not about code.

WHAT WAS RULED OUT FIRST, because 'not my code' is a claim needing evidence rather than an assumption. The suspicion was concrete: the detail page imports RecipeCard (page.tsx), and RecipeCard statically imports the new CardMacroLine, so the component looked like it should ride along. It does not. In the production build the chunk carrying CardMacroLine (1879-*) is in /recipes' first-load set and ABSENT from the detail route's, and searching all 33 of that route's first-load chunks for 'recipeCard.macroEstimated' returns 0 hits -- with 'useState' (18 chunks) and 'buttermilk' (6) as positive controls IN THE SAME COMMAND, so that is a true negative and not a search that silently failed. Webpack grouped the component into a chunk the detail route does not pull.

METHOD NOTE worth reusing, since 'my PR is red on a route it does not touch' recurs in this file. Answer it in one build: compare the route's chunk list in .next/app-build-manifest.json against a distinctive identifier from the suspected module, and ALWAYS carry a positive control in the same command -- an absent string and a broken search are indistinguishable otherwise, which is the trap //food-classifier-correction was written about. Then, before editing a claim, CHECK WHETHER THE SAME TREE READS DIFFERENTLY TWICE: had that been done here, the 310 edit would never have been written.
